metadata.audience: English-speaking independent visitors interested in maritime history, religious culture, Minnan life and ceramics, 2–4 days
metadata.promise: Quanzhou is a maritime system made visible in urban space; Dehua is one production chapter in that system. The product connects rather than collects them.
metadata.commercial_boundary: Research and human-checked digital roadbook only. No religious access promise, workshop/artist booking, product authentication, shipping, ticket resale, bundled travel or third-party experience sales.
metadata.point_decision_layer_ref: 泉州德化点位决策字段_V1.0.json

source_policy.rule: Religious access, rituals, ceremonies, museum/heritage operations, artist availability, ceramic quality and transport are dynamic. Use a dated human check; community materials are leads only.

sources.title: UNESCO: Quanzhou Emporium of the World

modules.name: A maritime system, not a monument list
modules.question: How did production, transport, belief and trade make Quanzhou a world port?
modules.output_rule: Connect 2–3 components through one system question, never all sites in a day.

modules.name: Religious plurality with etiquette
modules.question: How do I visit sacred sites without consuming belief as spectacle?
modules.output_rule: Use public access and written etiquette; verify current rules and exclude worship photography.

modules.name: Port, gate, bridge and river-sea movement
modules.question: Where does trade infrastructure become visible?
modules.output_rule: Use a public-space route linking city and water/transport ideas; field-check distance and access.

modules.name: Minnan public life and sound
modules.question: How can Nanyin, tea, food and streets add lived cultural context?
modules.output_rule: Separate observation/context from performance/class promises; no forced authenticity.

modules.name: Dehua: ceramics as production and design
modules.question: Do I want to understand a ceramic system, buy an object, or join a verified making encounter?
modules.output_rule: Separate production history, current design, buying and potential workshop.

modules.name: Ceramic purchasing and experience boundary
modules.question: How do I avoid confusing a route with authentication or an artist booking service?
modules.output_rule: Give questions and risk boundaries; no quality, provenance, price, shipping or availability promise.

modules.name: Quanzhou–Dehua pacing decision
modules.question: Does Dehua deserve a full separate day?
modules.output_rule: Yes unless a current short public visit is verified; never add casually to city heritage day.

modules.name: Arrival, weather and foreign-visitor friction
modules.question: Can the route work for actual dates, payment, transport and sacred/craft access?

points.name: Maritime-system framing card
points.why_it_matters: Quanzhou's value is the relationship between production, transport, marketing, institutions and social/cultural life, not an isolated temple count.
points.agent_use: Begin with one system question and choose only a few components.

points.name: Kaiyuan Temple decision
points.why_it_matters: A major sacred/heritage component that can introduce Buddhist, urban and maritime-era layers when approached with current etiquette and access rules.
points.agent_use: Do not promise entry or treat worship as performance.

points.name: Qingjing Mosque decision
points.why_it_matters: A key route into Quanzhou's transregional religious and trading connections, requiring a calm, context-led and etiquette-aware visit.
points.agent_use: Verify access and use religious literacy, not a diversity checklist.

points.name: Tianhou Temple decision
points.why_it_matters: A maritime-belief layer that can connect sailors, trade and community rather than being a generic temple stop.
points.agent_use: Check current practice and never interrupt ritual activity.

points.name: Sacred-site etiquette card
points.why_it_matters: Respectful travel requires quiet, consent and clear rules around dress, smoke, ritual, queues and photography.
points.agent_use: Deliver conduct guidance before sacred-site suggestions.

points.name: Deji Gate / urban-port decision
points.why_it_matters: A possible way to make the relationship between city gate, maritime trade and urban circulation visible.
points.agent_use: Pair only with a compatible system story and field-checked walk.

points.name: Luoyang Bridge decision
points.why_it_matters: A transport-infrastructure component that can reveal the wider water-land network beyond the old-city core.
points.agent_use: Treat as a separate half-day decision, not a default add-on.

points.name: Port-network public route lead
points.why_it_matters: A future route connecting water, gate, bridge and city may become a signature product after field distance/safety audit.
points.agent_use: Do not emit until field-tested.

points.name: Nanyin context/performance decision
points.why_it_matters: Nanyin can deepen a visit through sound and social transmission, but a visitor may seek context, a performance or a participatory class—three different products.
points.agent_use: No performance/class promise without current verification.

points.name: Minnan food/tea social geography
points.why_it_matters: Food and tea can reveal time, hospitality and neighbourhood life, but must not become an unverified restaurant ranking.
points.agent_use: Ask form, diet and pace; name no fixed venue without audit.

points.name: Public old-city walking ethics
points.why_it_matters: Street life is not a performance. A deep route uses public places and respects homes, worship and work.
points.agent_use: State public/private rules explicitly.

points.name: Dehua ceramic-system decision
points.why_it_matters: Dehua matters as a production, design, labour and distribution system, not simply a place to buy white porcelain.
points.agent_use: Ask learning, design, buying or making intent before a day trip.

points.name: Dehua public museum/showroom lead
points.why_it_matters: A potential public entry to material/process/design, subject to current access and language audit.
points.agent_use: No current venue claim until verified.

points.name: Verified ceramic-maker experience gate
points.why_it_matters: A maker visit can become a premium offer only after English, safety, consent, group size, payment/cancellation, photography and public-claim evidence exist.
points.agent_use: Capture interest; do not quote or book.

points.name: Ceramic purchase boundary
points.why_it_matters: A route cannot authenticate material, maker, provenance, price, food safety, export, shipping or insurance.
points.agent_use: Give independent-due-diligence questions only.

points.name: Two-day Quanzhou core
points.why_it_matters: Two days can hold one maritime-system thread, religious/public-space context and recovery; it cannot hold Dehua as well.
points.agent_use: Keep Dehua separate.

points.name: Three-day Quanzhou plus Dehua decision
points.why_it_matters: Only with a third day can Dehua become a deliberate production extension rather than a rushed shopping trip.
points.agent_use: Require field-verified transfer and current public access.

points.name: Arrival/payment/foreign-language audit
points.why_it_matters: Independent foreign travel depends on payment, data, rail/airport arrival, food communication and practical mobility.
points.agent_use: Ask arrival and readiness before Day 1.

points.name: Weather and sacred/craft contingency
points.why_it_matters: Rain, ritual access or maker availability can change a route; a humane product keeps a meaningful public alternative.
points.agent_use: Build a current-check alternative.

points.name: Inland/Maritime Fujian handoff
points.why_it_matters: Quanzhou should not be diluted into a rushed Fujian circuit; other destinations need separate databases and real transfer days.
points.agent_use: Do not package extensions or claim transport inventory.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you interested in trade systems, port infrastructure, religious exchange, ceramics production or all of these?
Do you want historical context, sacred architecture or living religious practice—and are you comfortable following strict etiquette and access limits?
Do you want production context, contemporary design, buying ceramics, or a verified making encounter?
Are you seeking contextual listening, a current performance, or a participatory class? Language and availability require verification.
Do you have two city days only, or a separate third day for a full Dehua decision?
What weather, walking, stairs or transfer threshold requires an alternative?
Would you like a human-checked brief with official links while you make any bookings directly?

output_guardrails: Never consume religion as spectacle or promise sacred access.
Never guarantee a performance, ritual, workshop, artist, maker, museum or current exhibition.
Never authenticate ceramic quality, provenance, value, export, shipping or safety.
Never add Dehua to a two-day Quanzhou core.
Never sell a user resource before it passes the experience release gate.
No booking, payment collection, packaging, guiding or third-party experience sales.

launch_checks.name: Old-city maritime-system walk
launch_checks.purpose: Distance, narrative coherence, weather and public/private ethics

launch_checks.name: Sacred-site etiquette/access audit
launch_checks.purpose: Current entry, rituals, photography and conduct

launch_checks.name: Dehua full-day production audit
launch_checks.purpose: Transfer, public access and maker release candidates
